beats.text: You finished the RTL. Now you need proof it matches the spec — before tape-out, not after a week of debug in the lab.
Open the SHA-256 accelerator. Real crypto hardware you're bringing to verification.
Attach the design files. Upload RTL and drop in the SystemVerilog core.
Attach the functional spec too. Every check should trace back to a requirement.
Tell Chipix to build a mental model. It reads the RTL and the spec before it writes a single line of test code.
Open the mental model. Walk the overview, modules, ports, parameters — what this block actually does.
That matches what you expect. Approve it and keep going.
Now Chipix writes the unit testbench — on screen, in your editor. Take a second. Skim the stimulus and the scoreboard as it lands.
Switch to Verify. Pick UnitSim, approve the plan, hit Implement — and the run card comes alive.
Watch the stages run. Two tests pass. The multi-block padding case fails — msg_last never fired on the last block.
Chipix names the bug and shows the fix in a diff. You click Apply. The patch lands in the testbench.
Run it again. All three UnitSim cases pass. Formal checks reset, handshake, and digest hold. Coverage moves up.
Verification complete. A real failure caught, a one-click fix applied, green across the board.
That's Chipix: read the design first, write tests in your IDE, run staged verification, fix what breaks — in one thread. If you're bringing up blocks like this every week, start here.
